html:
At Lindanise, on 15 June 1219, the army of King Valdemar II of Denmark beat the Estonians and took the hill fort on the site of Tallinn. It was a key step in the Northern Crusades against the last pagans of Europe.

German crusaders were already pushing into southern Estonia from Riga. The Danes built a castle on Toompea hill, and the town that grew below it became Tallinn, often explained as Taani linn, the Danish town. By legend the Danish flag, the Dannebrog, fell from the sky during the battle.

Within a few years all of Estonia was conquered and forced into Christianity. Danish, German, Swedish and Russian rulers followed one another until 1918, while a German-speaking nobility held the land. The Estonians rose in the St. George's Night Uprising of 1343. See Denmark.
